analysis.title: Where Things Stand
key_insights: The hedge fund unwind is very real and extended, but broader positioning remains elevated, the Fed has not eased, and the AI earnings debate is unresolved. Investors are frozen, finding it hard to add shorts or buy the dip.
GS prime fundamental L/S net leverage fell to 42.3%, the 1st percentile over the past year. Beta-adjusted net leverage fell more than 22 pts since early October to 48.2%, a five-year low.
SPX top of book liquidity fell to about $4mm, near YTD lows. Thin liquidity is likely contributing to the magnitude of realized vol.

The 6 week straddle discussed the prior weekend realized 2x over a 5 day period, and its price more than doubled from 4% to 8.2%. Convexity is trading at panic levels seen only in historic episodes such as 2025 liberation day, 2020 covid, 2022 and 2010-2011.
The author frames the period as an 'AI conviction crisis': capital intensity, financing needs, ROI and valuations are all being questioned at once, though the AI trade is not abandoned.

Commodities: copper is hit by macro sentiment as easy metal diversion blunts record Chinese tightness. Precious metals see an orderly deleveraging with CTAs still sellers. Oil escalation odds faded and macro caps rallies, with back end vol rich and put skew cheap.

GS vol panic index hit 9.8 out of 10 last Friday. Readings above 9.5 have historically signaled near-term relief, but the Fed is hiking this time, and in five hiking-regime episodes with panic above 9, subsequent three-month returns averaged just +0.4%.

Positioning is mixed outside HFs. The GS US Equity Sentiment Indicator is at the 75th percentile, equity MF and ETFs took in nearly $170bn since the start of Q4, and asset manager equity futures length is at the 82nd percentile.

Q4 2018 parallels: the October 2018 panic episode was followed by another 6.8% decline over three months. Versus 2018, equities (especially tech) are close, credit has barely moved, rates have done half the work, FX has outperformed massively, and havens (gold, JPY) moved the wrong way.
GIR's Ben Snider lists three bottom conditions: improved confidence in AI earnings trajectory, a better macro backdrop such as a dovish Fed signal, and a major decline in investor positioning.

VXN finished Friday at its highest level since COVID and VXSMH at its series all-time high, with the front of the vol curve sharply inverted. The desk argues vol has overshot without needing to call an equity bottom.
Desk preference is to underwrite volatility rather than chase stocks: sell puts at levels where adding length is acceptable, particularly in tech where the vol repricing is most extreme.

sector_views.rationale: Vol repricing is most extreme in tech and semis, so the desk prefers selling puts for entry over buying delta, while AI earnings uncertainty leaves room for more downside.

earnings_insights: AI earnings debate unresolved: capital intensity, financing requirements, ROI and valuations are being questioned simultaneously. No specific EPS or revenue figures cited.

trade_ideas.description: Sell puts on tech and semis names at levels where the desk would add length, underwriting elevated implied vol
trade_ideas.rationale: Paid considerably more to take equity risk, with the ability to add at lower entry levels if the unwind continues.
trade_ideas.risk: Still taking downside risk if this becomes a more sustained selloff.

tension_points.bull_case: Vol panic index at 9.8 with readings above 9.5 historically signaling near-term relief, and vol has overshot.
tension_points.bear_case: Broad positioning has not washed out, the Fed is hiking, and the Q4 2018 analog saw another 6.8% decline.
tension_points.what_invalidates: No dovish Fed signal, no improved AI earnings confidence, and no major decline in broad investor positioning, the three conditions GIR's Snider names for a bottom.
